name: cloud-keyboard
description: Cloud Keyboard — IME with on-device translation, voice input, and bundled sticker packs. Standalone constellation APK.

android._doc_version: version_code/version_name live here, not in app/build.gradle. libs/keyboard is shared by reference and reads ${rootDir}/build.json, so these are what the keyboard APK's BuildConfig reports - they used to resolve to aa_cloud-superapp's because the module read a relative path.

libs:keyboard._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ - settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. These paths used to be hardcoded as include/projectDir pairs in settings.gradle, which meant the module graph lived in two places and neither knew about the other. build.json is now the only place a module is declared.

modules._doc: Keyboard libs are shared from ../aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ via relative project references in settings.gradle.

libs:text-tools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/ - settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy.
libs:text-tools._doc: The ITextTools binder. This APK SERVES it: libs:keyboard holds AiRouter (Enhance) and reaches libs:translate (Translate), so it is the only app that can answer, and the only one that ever sees the provider key. cloud-mail declares the same module to CALL it.

keyboard_media._doc: Same block as aa_cloud-superapp — shared vault secret. build.sh sops-decrypts vault_secrets → TENOR_API_KEY/GIPHY_API_KEY env vars → Gradle BuildConfig → MediaRuntime.configure().

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps — the SAME key that signs the superapp, so the in-app fleet updater never hits INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, and _enforce_signature re-signs the built APK with it. NO fallback: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD — it never signs with the ephemeral android debug keystore.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh. Until this block existed ship-cloud-keyboard.yml called the publish gate and assembleRelease and nothing else: it never invoked the test engine at all, so the green it reported meant only that the Kotlin compiled. The assertions that DO cover this keyboard were filed under aa_cloud-superapp/test/ and gate the superapp's release, not this one — a keyboard could ship broken with every one of them passing.

shell._doc_requires: Tools a tester shells out to, checked BEFORE anything runs. A missing tool does not fail a tester, it makes the tester answer from the tool's absence: four testers in this repository passed only because ripgrep was not installed and their invocation failed open. Neither tester here uses ripgrep, deliberately. python3 is the silence guard itself; awk extracts the Kotlin function bodies the structural assertions read, and an absent awk would hand them empty bodies to agree with.
shell._doc_quarantine: Filename to the REASON it may fail. Empty, and it should stay that way: a quarantined tester that starts PASSING fails the build, so an entry cannot outlive its reason. Anything not named here is fatal.

unit._doc: No JVM unit tests exist in this app (0 files under */src/test/) and none can be written from the container that maintains it, which has no JVM. Left disabled rather than pointed at an empty task so the engine LOGS the gap on every run instead of printing a green tick for a suite that is not there.
